sectors.summary: XLK was the day's worst sector at -2.01%, driven almost entirely by a 2% drop in NVDA as AI-infrastructure names de-rated, while mega-cap software (MSFT +0.17%) and AAPL (+0.39%) held green. The split tape signals rotation out of high-beta semis and into lower-volatility compounders rather than a wholesale tech exit.

opportunity.reason: AAPL closed +0.39% against a 2% sector decline, showing clear relative strength and defensive bid as capital rotates out of AI-levered semis. Its hardware/services mix makes it the natural holding spot for tech exposure during an AI-trade unwind.

avoid.reason: NVDA's -2.01% drop led the sector lower and momentum is deteriorating ahead of a high-expectations earnings setup. Chasing the dip before the AI capex narrative stabilizes carries outsized gap risk.

sectors.summary: XLF gained 0.81% with broad participation, led by the money-center banks (BAC +1.01%, JPM +0.98%) as the rotation out of growth favored value and rate-sensitive balance sheets. Capital markets names lagged, with GS up only 0.32%.

opportunity.reason: BAC led the group at +1.01% and is the most rate- and deposit-beta-sensitive of the large banks, making it the cleanest vehicle for continued value rotation. Valuation remains a discount to JPM with similar credit trends.

avoid.reason: GS underperformed its peers today (+0.32% vs XLF +0.81%) and at $916 its trading/IB-heavy revenue mix is more correlated to the risk assets that sold off. Prefer traditional lenders over capital-markets beta here.

sectors.summary: XLE rose 0.98% with the E&P and refining-levered names leading (CVX +1.64%, COP +1.59%) while XOM lagged at +0.48%. Firmer crude plus the broader defensive/value bid kept the sector near the top of the leaderboard.

opportunity.reason: COP's +1.59% move shows upstream leverage to firming crude with the sector's strongest beta to price, plus a disciplined shareholder-return program. It is the preferred expression of continued energy momentum.

avoid.reason: XOM's +0.48% gain was only half the sector's move, showing persistent relative lag versus CVX and COP. With the integrated trade crowded, better risk/reward sits in the pure-play E&Ps.

sectors.summary: XLV added 0.54% in a quiet, broad advance with LLY (+1.26%) doing the heavy lifting and MRK/UNH posting modest gains. The sector is acting as a mid-tier defensive, outperforming tech but trailing staples and energy.

opportunity.reason: LLY was the clear sector leader at +1.26% and $1,443, maintaining an uptrend on sustained incretin demand that is insulated from the AI-trade unwind. Relative strength on a defensive day is a constructive continuation signal.

avoid.reason: UNH's +0.58% is a muted bounce given how much ground the stock has lost, and medical-cost-trend uncertainty continues to cap rallies. Wait for a durable base rather than buying incremental upticks.

sectors.summary: XLY fell 0.4% as high-multiple consumer names followed tech lower, with TSLA -1.82% the main drag and AMZN down 0.29%. Defensive big-box retail (HD +0.12%) barely held green, underscoring the day's risk-off tone within the consumer.

opportunity.reason: HD eked out a gain while the sector fell, offering the most defensive, dividend-supported consumer exposure during a growth de-rating. It also carries optionality to lower rates reviving home-improvement demand.

avoid.reason: TSLA's -1.82% decline made it the worst large-cap in the sector and it trades as a high-beta proxy for the same momentum complex that led today's selloff. Downside risk remains elevated until the growth tape stabilizes.

sectors.summary: XLP was the day's top sector at +1.42% with uniformly strong breadth (WMT +1.51%, COST +1.28%, PG +1.05%), a textbook defensive rotation signature. Money leaving semis and high-multiple discretionary clearly found a home here.

opportunity.reason: WMT led the strongest sector at +1.51%, combining defensive earnings visibility with genuine share gains and e-commerce margin expansion. It is the highest-quality way to ride the ongoing defensive rotation.

avoid.reason: COST participated (+1.28%) but at $1,106 it carries a premium multiple that leaves little cushion if the defensive bid fades or a soft comp print lands. Prefer WMT's better valuation-to-momentum tradeoff today.

sectors.summary: XLI slipped 0.39% as cyclical machinery and aerospace names failed to join the value rotation, with CAT -0.84% leading the decline and BA and HON roughly flat. The weakness suggests the rotation is favoring defensives and energy over capex cyclicals.

opportunity.reason: HON's near-flat -0.13% print held up far better than the heavy-machinery complex, and its aerospace-aftermarket and automation mix offers steadier cash flow in a slowing cyclical tape. It is the defensive choice within a weak sector.

avoid.reason: CAT fell 0.84% and was the sector's biggest drag, with its recent run tied to data-center/power capex that is wobbling alongside the AI trade. Momentum is rolling over at a stretched valuation near $600.

sectors.summary: XLB edged down 0.21% in a sharply split tape: FCX dropped 2% with the broader cyclical/momentum unwind while industrial gas LIN rose 0.68% and gold miner NEM gained 0.44%. Defensive and precious-metals exposure is outperforming base-metal cyclicality.

opportunity.reason: LIN rose 0.68% against a down sector, offering contracted, utility-like volume growth and pricing power that holds up when cyclicals wobble. It remains the quality anchor in materials.

avoid.reason: FCX was the sector's worst performer at -2%, tracking the same high-beta unwind that hit semis and reflecting softer copper sentiment. Avoid adding until base metals find a floor.

sectors.summary: XLRE was essentially unchanged at +0.02% as the group failed to capture the defensive bid flowing into staples and utilities. Internals diverged, with tower REIT AMT up 0.97% while mall operator SPG slipped 0.27%.

opportunity.reason: AMT's +0.97% move led the sector and towers offer long-duration contracted escalators that benefit most if rates drift lower. Its relative strength on a flat REIT day marks it as the group's leadership name.

avoid.reason: SPG fell 0.27% while rate-sensitive REITs rallied, signaling concern about the discretionary consumer that also pressured XLY today. Retail-landlord exposure is the weakest spot in the sector right now.

sectors.summary: XLC rose 1.05% but the strength was narrow and concentrated: META surged 2.9% while GOOGL fell 0.98% and NFLX slid 0.86%. The dispersion points to an intra-sector rotation out of recent winners into META rather than a broad bid.

opportunity.reason: META's +2.9% was the single strongest move among all listed mega-caps today, signaling capital rotating back into a name that had been discounted on capex concerns. Momentum plus reasonable earnings multiple make it the top near-term setup.

avoid.reason: GOOGL fell 0.98% even as its sector gained over 1%, a clear relative-strength breakdown after an extended run to $295. Profit-taking risk is elevated while flows favor META.

sectors.summary: XLU gained 0.52% on the defensive rotation, but leadership came from traditional regulated names (DUK +1.3%, SO +1.21%) while AI-power proxy NEE fell 0.2%. That split mirrors the broader de-rating of data-center-linked trades.

opportunity.reason: SO rose 1.21% on a classic regulated-utility bid, offering dependable rate-base growth and a solid yield as investors seek shelter from the tech selloff. Clean relative strength with low beta.

avoid.reason: NEE was the only major utility in the red (-0.2%) as its renewables and data-center-demand narrative tracks the weakening AI complex. It is the wrong utility to own if the power-for-AI trade keeps unwinding.
